quickAnswer: Packaged food brands in Alathur must synchronize food safety compliance with intellectual property protection before commercial distribution. Operating lawfully requires obtaining an FSSAI State License or Registration via FoSCoS and strictly following FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations. Protecting the brand name requires filing on Form TM-A under Class 29 (banana chips, fried tapioca, processed fruit snacks) and Class 30 (milled rice, flour savouries, spices, confectionery). Securing trademark clearance before printing retail packaging prevents costly inventory recalls.

h2Sections.h2: Alathur's Renowned Food Heritage: From Village Stalls to Supermarket Shelves
content: Alathur, situated in southern Palakkad along the foothills of the Western Ghats, has long enjoyed a celebrated reputation across Kerala for its traditional culinary craftsmanship. Most famously, the town is legendary for 'Alathur Chips'—crisp, thinly sliced banana chips fried in pure coconut oil with a distinct golden texture and seasoning that has made them a staple souvenir for travelers along the National Highway 544 transit corridor.

In recent years, traditional chip makers, rice millers, and local confectioners in Alathur have transitioned from informal roadside stalls into mechanized packaging units, distributing sealed pouches to supermarkets across Kerala and Gulf export markets. However, entering modern retail distribution requires complete regulatory compliance. Food operators must simultaneously navigate mandatory FSSAI food licensing, precise packaging declarations, and statutory trademark registration to protect their brand equity.

h2Sections.h2: The Mandatory Dual-Class Trademark Structure: Class 29 vs. Class 30
content: A frequent legal pitfall in the packaged food industry is filing under only one class while producing foods that span multiple statutory categories under the Nice Classification.
The table below details how Alathur packaged foods are categorized under Indian trademark law.

rows: Banana chips, fried tapioca chips, jackfruit crisps, roasted cashews, coconut oil, preserved pickles.
Milled Matta rice, rice flour, Kerala mixture, murukku, sharkkara varatti, spices, bakery biscuits.
Raw unprocessed paddy, fresh green bananas in bunches, raw agricultural seeds.
Operating packaged food retail outlets, highway snack kiosks, direct-to-consumer e-commerce websites.

content: Under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, selling packaged foods without an active FSSAI registration or license is a punishable offence carrying severe monetary penalties and confiscation of inventory.

1. Determining License Category: Micro food producers with annual turnover up to ₹12 Lakh require basic FSSAI Registration. Commercial manufacturing units, mechanized chip factories, and rice mills with turnover between ₹12 Lakh and ₹20 Crore must obtain an FSSAI State License via the FoSCoS portal.

2. Mandatory Pouch Labeling: All retail pouches must prominently display: the 14-digit FSSAI License number, FSSAI logo, exact commercial brand name, complete ingredient list in descending order of weight, nutritional facts panel, vegetarian logo (green dot), Net Quantity, Date of Manufacture, Expiry / Best Before Date, Batch number, and complete manufacturer name and premises address.
3. Trademark Symbol Usage: Display the ™ symbol next to your brand name once Form TM-A is submitted, switching to the registered ® symbol only after the official certificate is issued.

callout.title: Never Print Packaging Before Trademark Clearance
callout.text: Never order tens of thousands of custom-printed laminate snack pouches before conducting an IP India trademark clearance search. If the Trade Marks Registry rejects your mark or an established brand sends a cease-and-desist notice, your entire packaging inventory must be destroyed.

h2Sections.h2: Actionable Launch Checklist for Alathur Food Brands
content: Before shipping your packaged food products to retail distributors, complete this verified compliance checklist:
checklist: Conduct phonetic trademark clearance search on IP India across Class 29 and Class 30
Submit Form TM-A to the Chennai Registry using an Udyam MSME certificate to secure the ₹4,500 fee rate
Apply for FSSAI State License or Registration via the FoSCoS online platform
Audit pouch artwork to ensure compliance with FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations 2020
Obtain GST registration if annual business turnover exceeds statutory thresholds (₹40 Lakh for goods)
Maintain batch production registers, oil quality logs, and raw material sourcing invoices

h2Sections.h2: Frequently Asked Questions for Alathur Food Businesses
content:
Q: Can I register the name 'Alathur Chips' as my private trademark?
No. 'Alathur' is a geographical town name and 'Chips' is a generic food noun. Section 9(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act prohibits registering geographical place names as private trademarks. You can only protect a distinctive, coined brand name used alongside the geographic description (e.g., '[YourCoinedBrand] Alathur Chips').

Q: Does an FSSAI license grant ownership over our food brand name?
No. FSSAI is a food safety and public health regulatory authority. It does not grant intellectual property rights. Trademark ownership can only be secured through the Trade Marks Registry under the Trade Marks Act 1999.

Q: If our unit produces both banana chips and mixture, can we use one multi-class application?
Yes. You can file a consolidated multi-class Form TM-A covering both Class 29 and Class 30, paying the statutory fee for two classes (₹9,000 total for MSME/individual applicants).

faqs.question: Does an FSSAI license protect a food brand name from being copied?
faqs.answer: No. An FSSAI license certifies food safety and hygiene compliance, but provides zero intellectual property protection. Only a registered trademark provides exclusive legal ownership over your brand name.

faqs.question: Which trademark class applies to packaged banana chips?
faqs.answer: Banana chips, tapioca chips, and processed fruit snacks fall under Class 29, while flour-based snacks like mixture, murukku, and sweets fall under Class 30.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for selling packaged food without an FSSAI license?
faqs.answer: Operating a food business without a valid FSSAI license under Section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months and a fine up to ₹5 Lakh.
